notes: Evals for the team review phase. Tests the 4-mandatory-member contract, the regression-tester non-collapsibility rule, the markdown-only single-domain carve-out (S18 from RETRO #2), the severityCounts compute-helper requirement, and the regressionRun.skipped enum.

evals.name: four-mandatory-members-always
evals.prompt: You're invoked at review tier `recommended` with `agentTeamsEnabled: false`. List the 4 mandatory members and explain whether ANY can be skipped without recording a deviation.
evals.expected_output: 4 mandatory members: senior-engineer, software-architect, qa, regression-tester. NONE can be skipped without recording `consolidator.mode: in-line` AND a `globalWarnings[].kind: code-review-deviation` (or message-prefix variant) per the carve-out contract. regression-tester is non-collapsible even when other lanes consolidate inline — it always emits its own regressionRun payload.

evals.name: markdown-only-carveout-records-deviation
evals.prompt: The diff is exclusively `*.md` files (14 files), single domain `docs`, zero code-affecting findings upstream. You decide to use the inline-orchestrator carve-out instead of dispatching the 4 mandatory agents. Show the EXACT `consolidator` and `globalWarnings` JSON entries you must write.
evals.expected_output: `consolidator: { mode: "in-line", reason: "markdown-only single-domain (docs); 14 files; zero code-affecting findings upstream" }` AND a `globalWarnings[]` entry with `at: "<RFC3339>"`, `stepId: "STEP_<NN>_CODE_REVIEW"`, `message: "code-review-deviation: inline-orchestrator review used in lieu of 4 mandatory dispatches; markdown-only single-domain carve-out"`. The `kind`/`note` field shape is rejected by CUE — the schema's #GlobalWarning is closed `{at, stepId?, message}`.

evals.name: regression-run-skipped-only-no-test-setup
evals.prompt: Phase 5.0 — regression-tester returns `skipped: true` with `skipReason: "write-tests phase owns"`. Is this acceptable? If not, what's the ONLY valid skip reason, and what's the failure mode if you accept the bad reason?
evals.expected_output: REJECT — `"write-tests phase owns"` is explicitly banned (misleading: regression-tester's job is the LIVE blast-radius gate, not the post-fix test authoring). The ONLY acceptable skip reason is `"no-test-setup"` (paired with `tool: "skipped"`). Accepting the bad reason silently passes through code that breaks integration suites, since the regression gate never actually ran. The skill stops the step.

evals.name: severity-counts-computed-not-free-written
evals.prompt: You assembled 18 findings (1 high / 10 medium / 7 low). Show the bash that writes `codeReview.severityCounts` to the step. Cite the rule that bans free-writing the counts.
evals.expected_output: MUST use `compute_severity_counts` helper from `scripts/jq-helpers.sh`. Free-writing `{ high: 1, medium: 10, low: 7 }` directly is banned because the dogfood-report drift produced a payload claiming 1H/7M/19L when the live findings distributed 1H/10M/16L — the count and the source list disagreed. The post-write guard `assert_severity_counts $STEP_ID` then verifies no drift.
